en: The Dharma Gate of the Vairocana Ground-Mind for Accomplishing All Dhāraṇīs and the Threefold Siddhis of the Pure Dharmakāya.
At that time, the Buddha Vairocana was in the Lotus Treasury World, together with hundreds of thousands of billions...

The Transformation Body Śākyamuni Buddha taught the Chapter on the Purification of Conduct through the Precepts of the Mind-Ground, the Dharma for instructing Bodhisattvas and realizing the Path to Bodhi.
At that time, the hundreds of thousands of millions of Śākyas spoke with one voice, saying:
“World-Honored One, Lord of the Dharma!
Although all sentient beings have attained the Dharma-door of the mind-ground, they are unable to cultivate and study it with single-minded diligence;
even if they maintain mindfulness for a brief moment, they immediately abandon it, allowing their bodies and minds to run wild and acting at will in unwholesome ways.
Some may reflect:
"I have attained the profound and wondrous Dharma-gates of all Buddhas; how could I allow myself to regress through a lack of diligence? I shall instead resolve once more to seek the Way.
Thus, day and night they apply themselves with vigor, single-mindedly practicing and studying to seek the Unsurpassed Way.

There may be those who regress, further creating evil karma and entering the stream of birth and death; no longer contemplating the wondrous Dharma of the mind-ground, they transmigrate through the evil realms with no prospect of escape.
"How are such sentient beings to be tamed?
At that time, Vairocana Buddha addressed the hundreds of thousands of millions of Śākyamuni Buddhas, saying:
"Listen attentively now!"
I shall explain for you the Dharma of subduing, so that all sentient beings may universally attain peace and happiness.
Regarding the Dharma of the mind-ground, whether sentient beings have heard it or not, they shall all attain subduing: those who have heard it shall be urged to increase their diligent application;
those who have not heard it shall be inspired to resolve upon the Way.

"You should all know that when sentient beings attain the Dharma of the mind-ground, if they do not apply themselves with diligent effort but instead delight in committing various evils, [I] will create obstacles wherever they dwell, causing their bodies to be ill at ease."

These leaders of the assembly, being oppressed by suffering, will surely attain understanding through reflection, again give rise to the aspiration for the Way, and practice all forms of cultivation with diligent effort day and night.
Why is this? It is like a wild horse that will not be tamed; it can only be restrained by the application of whips and lashes.

Likewise, there are sentient beings who have not heard the Buddha-dharma; having inherited meager merit from previous lives, they have now obtained a human body and possess a meager supply of food and clothing. They delight in creating various worldly evil karmas and do not seek the causes for liberation and transcendence from the world.

These sentient beings have such rampant ignorance that they do not realize this body is like an illusion or a magical transformation, arising and dying in an instant; they do nothing but commit various evils, and upon death they enter hell, where they undergo all manner of bitter suffering with no prospect of escape.
The Buddha deeply pities such persons.

You should know that when these people are committing evil deeds, you must understand the method for subduing them: you should afflict them with severe illnesses from time to time so that no worldly methods can save them. When such sentient beings are thus oppressed by suffering, they will inevitably resolve to seek the Way; only then can they be guided and led into the Buddha-way.

When Śākyamuni heard these words, he felt shame and remorse; he prostrated himself in salutation, took his leave, and returned to his original world. Seated at the site of his bodhimanda, he reflected thus:

"The realm of the Buddhas is difficult to understand and difficult to enter, being inconceivable. They employ various skillful means to instruct sentient beings, yet ordinary people lack wisdom and are difficult to tame."
He further addressed the great assembly:

"You should all know that this Dharma-gate of the pure conduct of the *śīla* of the mind-ground is difficult to hear and difficult to see. All of you Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as the Śrāvakas, whether gods, nāgas, or spirits, should practice and study it with single-minded diligence, remembering and upholding it without forgetfulness; thus you shall attain Buddhahood."

At that time, the Great Wrathful Vajra rose from his seat, manifesting great marks and signs of excellence, and emitting inconceivable light that illuminated a hundred thousand lands. He prostrated in homage and addressed the Vajra, saying:

"Great Being, I have heard that when all Buddhas sit at the site of enlightenment, they universally praise the gateways of dhāraṇī and the essential principles of total retention (*saṃdhāraṇa*), establishing immeasurable and inconceivable matters that are beyond thought."
I reflect that among sentient beings, those with meager merit are many; even if some should uphold [this teaching], they will not achieve success.
I pray that the Great Being, for the sake of such people, will establish great skillful means so that they may attain accomplishment.
How should one attain the three kinds of *siddhi*?
How should one construct the nine kinds of mandalas?
How should one settle the body and mind while reciting the divine mantras?
How does one, from the very first recitation, perceive what signs arise and know for oneself that *siddhi* will be attained?
How should one select a place of residence?
How should one select one's food?
How should one perform various offerings?
How should one maintain all the proper dignified conducts (*īryāpatha*)—whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—and with what thoughts should one dwell?
For sentient beings who are impoverished and lack material things for offering, how should they maintain the visualization, and how may they attain *mahāsiddhi*?
Then Vajrapāṇi said to the wrathful Mañjuśrī:
"This may be asked of the Buddha; I am unable to answer.
Then the two Vajras addressed the Buddha with one voice, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The Buddha has spoken of the Dharma-gate of *dhāraṇī*; how should sentient beings practice and study it?
He asked each question in full, as detailed above.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the two Vajras, saying:
"You may pose this question to Vairocana Buddha; he will be able to know this matter.

Thereupon, the Buddha entered samādhi and exercised his supernormal powers, causing the entire assembly—including devas, nāgas, ghosts, and spirits—to arrive together in the Lotus Treasury World (Padmagarbha-lokadhātu), where they prostrated themselves in worship and said:
“O World-Honored One, the Dharma-body!

Among the sentient beings of this age, those who seek to uphold the essential points of the Dharma mostly fail; even if they achieve some slight merit, Vināyakas immediately create various obstacles and hindrances to cause their efforts to be frustrated.”
Furthermore, it causes those individuals to immediately give rise to their original nature, engendering a mind of weary detachment and the resolve to withdraw and renounce.

Such sentient beings, because they do not understand the wondrous Dharma of the Mind-ground—the realm of all Buddhas—fail to accomplish the three kinds of *siddhi* and instead become deluded and disturbed by ghosts and spirits.

We only pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion for all sentient beings and for our own sake, will explain the essential dharmas and the pure rules of conduct for upholding them; how may one attain the three kinds of siddhi?
"How should one settle the body and mind so that, while reciting mantras, one is not hindered by evil spirits and demons?
At that time, Vairocana Buddha said: "You should know this:

I recall in the past, when I first resolved to attain the Way, I was staying in an araṇya (hermitage), sitting upright in contemplation and practicing the Dharma-gate of the Mind-ground. Because I lacked wisdom, my mind was not stable, and all dharmas did not manifest before me."

Being thus unstable, various delusive thoughts arise and engage in objective attachments; for this reason, they are confounded and disturbed by ghosts and spirits, mistakenly entering the realm of Māra. Believing these to be the Buddha-dharma, they harbor greedy and affectionate desires, regarding them as the ultimate goal. Unaware and unknowing, they are harmed by Māra for incalculable kalpas.
Later, he suddenly regained his original mind and realized that this was demonic possession and not the Buddha-dharma.
Nevertheless, having no other recourse, he raised his voice loudly and addressed the Buddhas, saying:
"The Buddhas possess the eye of wisdom; why do you not see that I am being tormented by demons?"
At that time, countless transformation Buddhas in the air addressed me, saying:
"Excellent, Bodhisattva! Listen attentively now!

For your sake, I shall explain the method for dispelling Māras. There is a great divine mantra called the 'Dharmapada Mantra' (Heart-ground Mantra); those who recite and uphold it will swiftly attain all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā) and shall not be taken advantage of by any Māras."
Upon hearing these words, my heart was filled with great joy, and I said:
"I pray that all Buddhas will explain this for me.
Thereupon, the manifested Buddhas immediately explained it for me.
When I hear this and remember it without forgetting, all Māras will then retreat and disperse.
At that time, I shall attain the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti), and the Great Path of Bodhi will naturally become perfected.
You should know that regarding this Heart-Mind Ground Divine Mantra, there is no possibility for any Buddha to accomplish the Dharma of the Heart-Mind Ground without reciting this mantra.
It is impossible that one who sits at the site of enlightenment would not recite this mantra and remain free from all demonic obstacles;
it is likewise impossible for there to be any Buddha who does not recite this mantra yet possesses all-encompassing wisdom.
If one does not recite this mantra, the Sovereign of All Dharmas, there is no possibility [of success].
If any among gods or humans were to employ other mantras and yet attain *siddhi* without first reciting this mantra, there is no such possibility.
If one first recites this mantra, there is no possibility that subsequent mantras will fail to produce their effects.
There is no possibility that one who recites this mantra will be disturbed or harassed by Vināyakas.

Why is this? This mantra is the essential dharma of the mind-ground of all Buddhas. As for all mundane and supramundane dharmas, if they do not arise from the mind-ground, from what else could they be established?
"Therefore, none are able to enter the profound realm of the Buddhas.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha and the great assembly bowed their heads and addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"World-Honored One, we pray only that you will explain it."
At that time, Vairocana Buddha spoke the Heart-Mind Divine Mantra to Śākyamuni, reciting it as follows:

"Oṃ susthitavajra. Having spoken this mantra, celestial jewel-flowers rained down, and all the most sublime fragrant flowers and various musical instruments from the worlds of the ten directions gathered like clouds to offer worship. The music of the devas filled the air, and all the devas and nāgas exclaimed, "This is truly unprecedented!"
At that time, although the Buddha preached the Dharma, there were those in the assembly who heard it and those who did not. Why was this?

Those whose minds had attained liberation, those who had realized the three emptinesses, those who had obtained the Dharma-eye, those who had entered the realm of all Buddhas without fear, and those who were unimpeded regarding the dharmas of the mind-ground—all of them were able to hear it.
Those who well understand the skillful means taught by all Buddhas and who realize that all phenomena are like illusory appearances may also hear it.
Those who do not possess the wisdom described above do not hear it at all; they are like a drunken person who lies down after drinking wine and remains unaware and unconscious.

At that time, after Vairocana Buddha had spoken this mantra, he suddenly vanished and entered the pure dharma-realm as a single body, pervading the lands of the ten directions like the great void, without any distinction; the entire assembly could no longer see him.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha also followed Vairocana Buddha in entering the Dharma-realm as a single, identical true essence; likewise, the entire assembly could no longer see him.

At that time, five great bodhisattvas—Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteśvara, Maitreya, and Vajragarbha—along with their retinues, attended upon Śākyamuni as they entered the profound dharma-realm to hear the Buddha Vairocana expound the gate of the essential teachings on the mind-ground and its most profound states.
The entire assembly was completely unaware of where their original teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha, and the great bodhisattvas were at that time.

Meanwhile, Vairocana Buddha, abiding within the pure dharmadhātu, entered a state of non-locality and, together with only five great bodhisattvas, taught the dharma-gate of the ritual rules, deportment, and signs of *siddhi* for the mantra of the Mind-Ground (*cittabhūmi*).
The Buddha addressed them, saying:

"You should all know that if you wish to study meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and wisdom (*prajñā*), enter all *samādhis*, and realize the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), you must first recite this Earth-Mind Mantra (*citta-bhūmi-mantra*) one million times. Once this is completed, sit in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka-bandha*), with your right hand pressing upon your left. Close your eyes and contemplate the absence of any fixed location; sever all thoughts yet do not depart from thought, sever all conditions (*pratyaya*) yet do not depart from condition. First contemplate that the four great elements (*mahābhūta*) and the five aggregates (*pañca-skandha*) are non-existent. Having performed this contemplation, recite this Earth-Mind Mantra twenty-one times, and you will spontaneously enter immeasurable *samādhis* and attain the patience of the non-arising of phenomena. Those who realize such a state know that it is ineffable."

When reciting this mantra, do not allow the mouth, tongue, or throat to move; rather, contemplate it with the mind, and furthermore, one must enter into the state of "mindfulness without thought"—this is called true mindfulness.
He addressed them, saying:

"You should know that for those who delight in the Mahāyāna and cultivate meditative concentration and wisdom, if there are those of dull faculties who lacked causes in past lives and are unable to settle their minds according to the preceding sequence, they need only recite the Heart-Mind Divine Mantra a full one million times; then the wisdom of their own nature will open, and they will swiftly realize the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*)."

If one has previously practiced and studied but has temporarily forgotten their former wisdom, there is no need for further extensive recitation; simply rely on the previously established mental ground and recite twenty-one times, and one will immediately attain meditative concentration and wisdom.
This person is able to enter all realms without fear; the perfection of prajñāpāramitā is spontaneously fulfilled, and only those who realize such a realm know it.
He further said:

"If among you there are those who uphold the divine mantras of the three sections and wish to achieve the realization of this Heart-Mind Ground Divine Mantra through the assistance of the Dharma, I shall now analyze and explain it for you."
Those who uphold the mantras of the Buddha Family should first recite the Heart-Mind Mantra one million times;
those who uphold the mantras of the Bodhisattva Family should recite the Heart-Mind Mantra two million times;
and those who uphold the mantras of the Vajra Family should recite the Heart-Mind Mantra three million times.
If a person merely fulfills this required number of recitations, they will achieve success regardless of which root mantra they maintain.

Why is this? Because this Heart Mantra is the mother of all mantras; therefore, the deities of all mantras dare not oppose it. If whatever one undertakes does not accord with one's wishes, one need only mentally recite the Heart Mantra twenty-one times, and a great efficacy shall be obtained: all the deities of the mantras will hasten and rush forth, none daring to disobey or fail to comply with one’s commands and dispatches.
He further said:

"You should know that if a person who upholds the mantras of the three sections has not yet attained siddhi, it is because they are an ordinary being for whom ignorance is rampant; they suddenly give rise to thoughts of regression, commit various unrighteous acts, become greedily attached to the five desires, and cause their recitation of the upheld mantras to be interrupted."
After a long period of time, they may suddenly and spontaneously awaken to the Bodhicitta and once again uphold the original mantra.

For their sake, I shall expound this "Mantra of the Mind’s Fundamental Merit" so that all sentient beings may possess an uninterrupted nature, remaining identical to the original state without regression.
He then spoke the *kṣema-karī* mantra, saying:

“Namo bhagavate uṣṇīṣāya oṃ bṛndanandaye svāhā | Tathāgatasaṃbhave svāhā | Padmanibhasvare svāhā | Vajranibhasvare svāhā | Maṇi maṇi maṇi kule svāhā | Tadyathā | Hūṃ phaṭ | Maṇidari hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ ga ga phaṭ | Maṇivajri hūṃ phaṭ. “This is the *kṣema-karī* divine mantra; it is also called the Root Mind-Ground Divine Mantra, and it is capable of extinguishing grave offenses.”
This karmic evil can be entirely extinguished by reciting this mantra.

It can also neutralize the efficacy of all other mantras and restore their own power; there is no need for further elaboration, for those who maintain its recitation shall obtain immeasurable results.

If a person who maintains a dhāraṇī interrupts their practice midway and wishes to resume it, they should first recite the original dhāraṇī according to their capacity for a certain number of times. Then, with sincerity, they should make a vow and prostrate before Vairocana Buddha, saying:

"I, disciple [Name], previously recited [Name] Dhāraṇī for [Number] recitations, but interrupted it midway. Now I have again recited it for [Number] recitations. I beseech all Buddhas to grant me the merit of my previous recitations as well as those of this present time, so that they may be unified and continuous without interruption."

He then recited the "Sū-gong" divine mantra one thousand and eight times, and again made a vow identical to the previous one; it was exactly the same as his original, non-regressive vow, without any difference.
Vairocana said: "Maintain this mantra and do not let it circulate among those who lack wisdom. Why is that?"

These ignorant people, seeing these teachings spoken by the Buddhas as skillful means, give rise to craving and indolence; they fail to exert diligent effort, conceive thoughts of the five desires, and retreat from their resolve for bodhi.

Why is this? Because such a person’s faculties are not firm and their wisdom is meager; having entered the stream of birth and death, even if they were to practice and study further, it would ultimately be of no benefit.
Why is this? It is like a person who takes a new garment and stains it with filth; later, when they wash it again, why was it not stained originally?
This mantra is also like that.
"If one is originally non-retrogressive, by reciting this mantra, they will assist the Dharma to be swiftly accomplished.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the World-Honored One, the Honored One of the Dharma-World, saying: "World-Honored One!"
Regarding the practitioner who holds the mantra and seeks the signs of the three kinds of *siddhi*, what are they? What are the signs of the superior *siddhi*?
What are the signs of the middling *siddhi*?
"What are the signs of the lower siddhi?

We pray only that the World-Honored One will explain them for us, so that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as humans and devas, may universally attain accomplishment, obtain the great samādhi of the stage of non-retrogression, realize the path to bodhi, achieve equal and perfect enlightenment, deliver the multitudes of devas and humans, cause them to enter nirvana, forever leave birth and death behind, and no longer undergo any suffering."
At that time, Vairocana Buddha said:
"If you wish to know the three kinds of *siddhi*, I shall explain them for you.

You should know that the characteristics of the superior, middling, and inferior *siddhis* are common to all three families; furthermore, each of the three families possesses its own three kinds of *siddhi*."

If there are good sons or others who wish to attain the supreme *siddhi*, they must maintain purity and protect both the internal and external spheres. Having purified the three actions of body, the four of speech, and the three of mind so that their afflictions and karma are cleansed, they should first recite the mantra they uphold until the number of recitations prescribed in the root scripture is fulfilled. Then, having also completed the required number of recitations for the *Cittabhūmi-mantra*, they should sit in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*) upon a seat of clean grass in a quiet and secluded place.

There, burning sublime incense as an offering, they should make vast and great vows, saying: "I announce to the Buddhas of the ten directions, the great Bodhisattvas, the great Vajradharas, and all the celestial beings, spirits, officials, and holy sages: may you all universally bear witness that I, disciple [Name], desire to receive and uphold this mantra."
"May the World-Honored One, the Bodhisattvas, Vajradhara, and the Devas truly bear witness that I may swiftly attain accomplishment.

Having made this vow three times, he immediately closes his eyes and sits. First, he recites the mantra he maintains eight hundred times. He then visualizes his own body as the body of the deity of this very mantra, with each and every limb adorned with the marks and signs of excellence (*lakṣaṇa* and *vyañjana*). Whether the body emits light or not, whether it is seated or standing, and its gestures of anger or joy—each detail is to be visualized according to the adornments of the painted image in the original sūtra. Having performed such contemplation, he must ensure that his own body is perceived with extreme clarity and distinctness.

Next, one should visualize immeasurable deities, clans, and messengers surrounding [the practitioner] before and behind, reverently attending upon them; visualizing each according to what is taught in their respective original lands, this contemplation will be grand, harmonious, and clear.

Having completed this, one should recite the dhāraṇī held in mind twenty-one times. With each repetition, light in the form of script and patterns issues from one's own mouth and enters the mouths of the deities.
Once the light has entered and ceased, one should visualize all the deities entering again collectively through one’s own mouth and being placed within the heart-king (*cittarāja*).
Visualize this three times a day; it must be done with clarity. If one practices this in sequence every day for a full twenty-one days, one will certainly attain the supreme *siddhi*.

Thereafter, not only will the matters described in the original scripture be fulfilled, but one’s intention to perform all manner of inconceivable deeds shall also achieve success. Whatever actions, intentions, gestures, or movements one undertakes, by means of this single type of fundamental mantra, one shall attain great mastery; this cannot be fully described.
When practitioners understand this, whenever they wish to perform any action, they should constantly reflect and think:

"I am the body of a Great Sage endowed with sovereign mastery; for now, I shall manifest as an ordinary person among the common folk to deliver suffering sentient beings, remaining unrecognized by others."

If one requires the various deities as messengers, one should visualize that from the sovereign of one’s own mind, ten billion trillion beings are emanated, surrounding one before and behind, abiding to carry out various commands without obstruction.
This is not due to human effort, but is the power of the Heart-Mind Divine Mantra, which is able to cause all deities to merge with the sovereign consciousness into a single entity.
Therefore, know this: if one maintains the mantras of the Buddha family or the Bodhisattvas, one shall attain the supreme siddhi;
however, if one maintains the mantras from the Vajra family downward, one shall not attain the supreme siddhi.

Why is this? Because the mantras of the Vajra devas and yakṣas are by nature fierce and cruel; if one were to achieve the supreme siddhi through them, one would attain mastery and thus fail to give rise to compassion, harming all spirits and deities.
If one can give rise to great compassion, universally pitying all beings without harboring a harmful intent or feeling anger, then one may freely attain the supreme *siddhi*.
Know this: if you cannot act as described, do not violate the flow of the Buddha’s words; otherwise, you shall incur great sin.
If one who upholds the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mantra attains the supreme siddhi, they are of one kind with all Buddhas.

Why is this? Although their body remains that of an ordinary person, their mind has attained mastery; their eloquence is unimpeded and their wisdom is unhindered. They are able to serve as teachers for all devas, humans, and the world, possessing all-encompassing knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) and all supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), such that their teachings can never be exhausted.
Therefore, one should know that they are no different from the Buddha.
There are further inconceivable matters that cannot be fully described; only those who have realized them know them.

If a practitioner of the Bodhisattva section attains the supreme *siddhi*, then by reciting their own root mantra, they become of one kind with the Bodhisattva who originally taught that mantra, without any difference whatsoever.

Why is this? By taking this mind of an ordinary person and adorning it with various skillful means—the power of the Bodhisattva’s transport and the power of mantras—one causes this ordinary person to attain a mind of one kind with that of a Bodhisattva.

Bodhisattvas possess ten thousand practices for the benefit of sentient beings, as well as supernormal powers and great mastery; those who maintain this mantra shall likewise attain all such qualities. One should know that they are in every respect identical to Bodhisattvas, with no difference between them, as they protect and uphold the Buddha-dharma and subdue all demons.
If one attains the supreme siddhi by upholding the Vajra-mantra, it is likewise identical to the single category of Dharma-vajra mentioned previously. Why is this?

Because "vajra" refers to an indestructible body; the person who upholds the mantra remains undestroyed in both body and mind, and the spiritual power they obtain is no different from that of the Vajra-mantra mentioned in the original teaching.

One who upholds this dhāraṇī can protect and maintain the Buddha-dharma, subdue all māras, and cause others to enter the right path; those who recite this spell can achieve all such things—yet are there further matters besides these?
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the World-Honored One,
the Lord of the Dharma: "World-Honored One,
those who uphold the mantras of the three families and achieve siddhi each obtain a form identical to their respective tutelary deity."
"How is it that ordinary beings (pṛthagjana) can thus obtain the vajra-body of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas while remaining among the ranks of ordinary folk?
Vairocana Buddha replied to Samantabhadra:
"You should know this: when the Buddhas manifest as ordinary beings, they may truly appear as ordinary beings; likewise, it is so for those who hold mantras and attain siddhi."
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
“O World-Honored One, Master of the Dharma!
We have already understood the supreme siddhi; what is the middling siddhi?”
"I only pray that you will explain this, so that all sentient beings may attain peace and happiness.
Vairocana Buddha replied to Mañjuśrī:
"As for the middling siddhi, according to the recitation of the mantras of the three families, there are respective methods for painting the images of their tutelary deities."

Furthermore, one should clearly visualize each detail as described in the original sūtra—the adornments of the body’s parts, as well as the various retinues and attendants—reciting them until the prescribed number of repetitions is fulfilled.
Then, according to the previous method, one should also recite the Heart-Ground Spirit Mantra until its full quota is reached. This may be done either in the mountains or in a vast wilderness.
Whether within city walls or marketplaces, inside monasteries or private dwellings, one must seek a secluded and quiet place—
be it an open space or within a room— and sit in stillness, burning various famous incenses to make offerings to all Buddhas,
Bodhisattvas, Vajras, devas, and the deity of this mantra. Then, immediately:
Having made great vows of repentance for the sins committed in previous lives as well as those created in the present,
and having dwelt in deep-hearted remorse and prostrated to the Triple Gem, one should immediately sit in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*), hold a rosary in hand,
close the eyes to fix the mind in concentration, and contemplate the deity and other spirits as if they were standing directly before one.
Stand facing [the deity] and perform this visualization with clarity.

Once the visualization is accomplished, recite the mantra you maintain eight hundred times; do so solely in the mind without moving the lips or tongue. With each repetition, visualize white light emerging from your own mouth and entering the mouth of the deity of the root mantra, ensuring that the light remains uninterrupted.
Once the recitation of the mantra is completed, one must clearly visualize the light from the mouth of the mantra-deity without interruption.

When the recitation is finished, one should again make aspirations, perform the mudrās for incense and flowers, and complete the offerings; then, immediately rising, one should prostrate and dismiss the deity according to the ritual rules.
In this manner, practicing three times during the day and three times at night—following these intervals for each session—for a full seven days, one accomplishes the middling *siddhi*.

If a person maintains the divine mantras of the three families and attains this middling *siddhi*, it will be great and inconceivable; all the efficacious powers described in the original sūtra shall be successfully realized.
Those who achieve success within the Buddha Family achieve it in all three families;

those who achieve success within the Bodhisattva Family achieve all the mantras of the various bodhisattvas, as well as the mantras of the devas, yakṣas, ghosts, spirits, and so forth from the Vajra Family downward, none of which fail to be accomplished;

and those who achieve success within the Vajra Family accomplish not only their own specific rites, but all the mantras of the vajras and below, including those of the devas, nāgas, ghosts, and spirits.
The mantra of the Bodhisattva does not become a Buddha-mantra, and the Vajra-mantra does not become a Bodhisattva-mantra.

Why is this? That which extends from the heart to the crown of the head is the upper [part]; that which extends from the navel to the heart is the middle; and that which extends from here to the navel is the lower.

Therefore, all dharmas cannot be practiced in reverse; one who maintains mantras must clearly distinguish between superior, middling, and inferior mantras. Know that this is the *siddhi* ritual procedure taught for all three families.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva addressed the World-Honored One, the Teacher of the Dharma:
"World-Honored One, the middle-siddhi has already been understood; what, then, is the lower siddhi?"
Vairocana Buddha addressed them, saying:

"You should know that if a person upholds the divine mantras of the three families and wishes to attain the lower siddhis, they must first recite the prescribed number of times and recite the Heart-Mind Mantra; the divine mantras are to be explained according to what was previously stated."

Once the full number of recitations has been completed, sit in a quiet place and burn agalloch incense as an offering. Then, recite the mantra of the Great Wheel Vajra Seal twenty-one times and prostrate, declaring:

"I pray that the Vajra may swiftly descend here. This disciple, in maintaining this mantra, seeks such-and-such a wish and desires to attain great accomplishment. Because this disciple, [Name], is impoverished and lacks all offerings, I pray only that the Great Sage will, for this disciple, lay out the Great Maṇḍala Dharma Altar here, following every detail according to the sūtra, without allowing anything to be omitted."
Having spoken these words, he closed his eyes and sat, visualizing the Vajra before him as having laid out a great maṇḍala altar, with the most exquisite objects serving as offerings.

Having visualized this maṇḍala, one next visualizes that the four walls and the ground are all composed of the seven treasures. Thereupon, one forms the hand-seal (*mudrā*), whereupon the various mantra-deities descend into the site of practice (*maṇḍala*). Having offered worship to the disciples and completed one hundred and eight recitations of the mantra one maintains, one personally makes a vow. In this manner, during the six periods of day and night, one visualizes each stage clearly and in succession for a total of fourteen days; thus, the lower *siddhi* is accomplished.
"Visualize this *maṇḍala* and its altar with perfect clarity; do not perceive them erroneously.
Vairocana Buddha declared:

"The thousand-billion emanations of Śākyamuni Buddha, along with the five great bodhisattvas and others—these are the signs of the accomplishment of the three kinds of *siddhi*. If a person upholds the divine mantras of the three families and attains these three *siddhis*, you should know that such a person will attain Buddhahood before long."

Why is this? This is the great skillful means of all Buddhas, the most essential teaching that expounds the gateway of dhāraṇī; its profound realm is difficult to understand, difficult to enter, and inconceivable.
He further addressed him, saying:
"The powers and virtues possessed by one who has attained siddhi cannot be fully described; only those who have realized them know them. Why is this so?"
If I were to explain this Dharma-gate in its entirety, some who hear it would have their minds become deranged and, filled with doubt, would not believe it. Why is this?
The realm of all Buddhas and the stage of Equal Enlightenment cannot be known as they truly are; how much less could ordinary devas avoid being struck with terror?
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva rose from his seat and addressed the World-Honored One, the Teacher of the Dharma:

"World-Honored One, the Tathāgatas take great compassion as their foundation. Why, then, do these various dhāraṇīs speak of wielding malice, possessing sovereign majesty and power to harm spirits, deities, heretics, and asuras?"
Vairocana said: "Listen attentively now!
I shall explain it for you."
There are two meanings here that one should understand well. What are these two?

First, the various Buddhas employ skillful means to preach the Dharma and guide sentient beings; second, they manifest this body of fierce and evil conduct to subdue all demons and cause them to enter the Buddha-way.

You should know that this, too, is a skillful means (*upāya*). When a mantra-practitioner encounters such circumstances, they may immediately give rise to anger in their heart to subdue spirits and deities;

yet, if they have not attained *siddhi*, the rite will not yield its fruition. Furthermore, they do not understand that these are spoken as skillful means by the Buddhas. To understand this: the various inverted thoughts, forgetfulness, and攀緣 (*pān-yuan*, clinging to objects) of one's own mind—which produce all manner of unwholesome acts—give rise to the mind of a hungry ghost (*preta*), or the mind of a non-Buddhist (*tīrthika*), or the mind of an asura, or the mind of various evil spirits, ghosts, and *rākṣasas*. For this reason, what arises moment by moment are all these evil spirits, devas, asuras, and various non-Buddhists, *rākṣasas*, and ghosts, which necessarily arise from the mind; though they do not immediately manifest, they receive such retribution.

Regarding what is taught in the various dharmas concerning the subduing of ghosts and spirits: by the power of this mantra, one can extinguish such evil thoughts within the mind; because one does not receive an evil body when these evil thoughts are absent, one should know that this is what constitutes "subduing."

If one can first subdue the various evil spirits within one’s own mind, then all celestial Māras, followers of external paths, devas, asuras, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and other evil spirits will naturally submit and obey, none daring to resist.
However, it is impossible for one who does not subdue their own evil mind to subdue other celestial beings and spirits.
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke again, saying:

"How is it that within the Dharma it is taught that one should treat illnesses and save sentient beings from suffering, yet in other sections of the sutras it is stated that the compounding of medicinal decoctions for the sick is not permitted? What is the meaning of this?"
Vairocana Buddha said:
"The treatment of illness is likewise; it does not differ from what was previously stated.
If one can cure the diseases of the mind, one will be able to cure all illnesses."
If one were personally afflicted by illness yet could cure that illness in another, such a thing is impossible.
When it is said that holding this mantra for the sake of curing one's own illness is not permitted, it is because of the practitioner's own sickness;
when it is said that there are those for whom it is permitted, it is because the power of this mantra causes the mind of the one being liberated to be free from illness.

One who has illness cannot be called liberated; a mantra-practitioner who possesses mental afflictions will ultimately be unable to cure various diseases, and even if they were to treat them, it would be impossible.
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke again:
"World-Honored One!
How is it that hearing this dhāraṇī can extinguish heavy offenses and also rescue one from the sufferings of hell? What is the meaning of this?"
Vairocana said: "There are two meanings to this:
first, true hearing; second, ear-hearing."

A true hearer deeply penetrates the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) and knows that all things are like illusions; the essence of sin is likewise thus, being utterly ungraspable. Such a person is a true siddhi who can save those in hell—how could one find it strange?

As for those who hear with their ears, they hear through the convergence of various causes and conditions. By this skillful means, the Buddhas cause these listeners to gradually cultivate and refine the inherent nature of their own consciousness. Through these causes and conditions, their manifold sins are extinguished; likewise, by relying on the power of the Buddhas, they are rescued from the sufferings of hell.
Vairocana Buddha said:
"If a person is unable to accomplish the three kinds of *siddhi*, yet can recite the Heart-Mind Divine Mantra one million times, the mantra they maintain shall surely yield great efficacy."

"If those who uphold various mantras act contrary to the Dharma and provoke the wrath of their original mantra-deities, they shall recite the *Cittabhūmi* (Heart-Ground), and all [deities] will naturally rejoice.

At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Vajragarbha-rāja Bodhisattva, and Maitreya Bodhisattva spoke in unison with these verses to praise Vairocana Buddha:
"The Buddhas are inconceivable, And the profound Dharma is likewise.
Now that I have heard this, I likewise understand its profound meaning:
The Dharma-body does not speak of a body; the Reward-body and the Response-body are likewise so.
When all three bodies do not speak, this is called the true meaning of speaking.
Whether spoken or unspoken, all is empty; it is neither one nor two.
Both the speaker and the listener—all these are of the nature of an illusion.
Like an illusion, they cannot be apprehended; such is the Buddha’s skillful means.
After these bodhisattvas had spoken this verse, they sat down to listen to the Dharma.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

For those who seek siddhi and, while reciting dhāraṇī-mantras in deep mountains or vast wildernesses, have not yet attained accomplishment and lack sufficient provisions for food, it is for this reason that they may cause them to retreat from the mind of bodhicitta.
"I shall now, for the sake of these good sons, proclaim the divine kitchen deity mantra.
He then spoke the mantra:

*Namo hradaṇa-dharanaya-jara-mahājara-tu-lu-maha-tulu-hūṃ jīva-hani-śe oṃ jīva-hani-śe śu.* "First, wash the bowl with pure water and place it upon a clean cloth. Then, place pure ash beneath the cloth and spread the cloth over the ash. Holding water in the mouth, sprinkle it upon the bowl; close your eyes and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times, while mentally visualizing the sublime celestial cuisine."
At that time, the devas sent celestial youths to present exquisite and superior food, which filled his alms bowl.

He then rose, prostrated before the World-Honored One Maitreya, and next paid homage to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. He then partook of the meal, distributing the remainder as alms to all the vast multitude of sentient beings.
If a person eats together with others and cannot finish the food, yet obtains this food to eat, they will naturally realize *siddhi*.

If one recites this mantra twenty-one times over human food and drink and gives it to hungry ghosts (*preta*), the ghosts who receive this food will be freed from the suffering of the hungry ghost realm and attain rebirth in the celestial palace of Maitreya.
If one reaches a year of famine, by reciting this mantra over human food and drink one thousand and eight times, it may be eaten by all people such that it shall never be exhausted.

In years of famine, on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon when it is full, one should burn incense, look up toward the sky, gaze at the moon, and recite this mantra one thousand and eight times while thinking:
"May all sentient beings illuminated by the moonlight obtain universal satiation, free from any thought of hunger or thirst."
On the fifteenth day at noon, one may also recite the mantra; make vows as prescribed above.
Every day, recite this mantra one thousand and eight times and make this vow:

"O Heavenly Kings and others, by means of these remaining offerings, may you dispatch the various heavenly deities to provide food for all the hungry ghosts throughout the worlds of the ten directions, so that once they have eaten, they shall be freed from their suffering."
"If a person can perform this rite every single day for three years without omission, its benefits will be vast and manifold.

After casting off this body, they shall be reborn in the Western Pure Land; during their present life, they shall increase their merit, and all other dhāraṇīs they uphold shall be fully accomplished."
At that time, Vajragarbha-rāja Bodhisattva said:
"When sentient beings uphold the mantras of the three families but have not yet attained accomplishment, they may still possess some slight efficacy, which serves as protection."
He then spoke the mantra: "Tadyathā oṃ vajrasvaya svāhā.

"If a person who upholds this mantra feels any unease, they should know that it is due to the harassment of various māras and yakṣas. They should immediately recite this mantra with urgency. I, together with the Kings of the Ten Directions and their retinues, will go to that place to provide protection. All the yakṣas, māras, and hosts of devils will be struck with panic and die; even if they regain consciousness, they will flee far to other regions and dare not remain there."
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent!
You bodhisattvas, by being able to inquire about these matters for the sake of all beings and by proclaiming this divine mantra, cause all sentient beings everywhere to receive peace and happiness."
He further said:

"All you should know that this profound sutra, the Dharma-gate of the Mind-Ground, has been taught by immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; it is difficult to encounter and difficult to hear."

If there are persons who, throughout immeasurable kalpas in the past, have made offerings to the Buddhas, deeply delighted in the Buddha-dharma, and felt weary of and detached from the cycle of birth and death in the world; and who, having previously heard the profound Dharma taught by the Buddhas, now for the first time hear this *Cittabhūmi Sūtra* and its *dhāraṇī*, and furthermore recite it with diligent and single-minded devotion—such persons as these are truly the children of the Buddha.
Why is this? Because before long, this person shall attain unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).

You should know that this sutra is the king among all sutras, and this mantra is the king among all mantras. You, all you Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, must propagate it throughout Jambudvīpa to bring great benefit and happiness to all sentient beings, so that those who hold this mantra may swiftly achieve *siddhi*.
At that time, Vairocana Buddha said:
"In disseminating this sutra, first observe their faculties and dispositions, and only then entrust it to them. Why is this?

Those with wisdom, upon hearing this, will believe it deeply; those without wisdom will surely give rise to alarm and fear, and further harbor doubts, causing those beings to instead incur their own transgressions and enter hell after death—receiving such retribution for slandering this sutra and the Buddhas.
While this sutra was being preached, the assembled multitude did not hear it, as it was spoken within the pure dharma-realm (dharmadhātu).

At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha and the five great bodhisattvas, having prostrated themselves before Vairocana Buddha, took their leave and proceeded to the Bodhi tree in Jambudvīpa to preach the Dharma for the assembly.
After this, following his parinirvāṇa, [the teaching] was entrusted to five great bodhisattvas and circulated throughout the world.

Because the śrāvakas had not heard the Buddha’s discourse, when they saw the assembly of bodhisattvas disseminating this sutra, they were deeply startled and filled with doubt; they did not believe it and did not accept it.
Then Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva said:

"You śrāvakas, this sutra is not within your domain, nor is it what you can know; it was spoken by Vairocana Buddha, along with the thousand billion transformation bodies of Śākyamuni and the great bodhisattvas. Therefore, it is not something you can know."
At that time, the great assembly heard this together; having heard it, they wept with grief and marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence.
Then the gathered multitude rejoiced, accepted it with faith, prostrated, and practiced accordingly.
